deep.reconstruction: This page has no mathematics. It is an administrative note in German in another hand, apparently a slip later reused as scrap paper by Gauss. The facing side (previous page) holds his cyclotomy calculations. As far as it can be read, the text says roughly: 'Alles, was in die Astronomie u. die verwandten Fächer einschlägt, ist ganz dem Hrn Prof. Gauss zur Besorgung überlassen; die Sammlung aber (?) kann er an Hrn Prof. Harding überlassen u. abgeben, auch (?) die verabredeten oder zu stiftenden [...]'. It is dated '3 Jun.' and initialled with a single letter, probably 'H'. In substance, everything belonging to astronomy and related subjects is left wholly to Professor Gauss to manage. A collection (perhaps of instruments, books or observatory material) may be handed over to Professor Karl Ludwig Harding, together with agreed or still-to-be-founded items. This fits Gauss's early Göttingen years (from 1807) as director of the observatory, with Harding as his colleague. The initial might be C. G. Heyne, who as head of the university library handled such matters until 1812, but this is only a conjecture. There is no derivation to reconstruct.

results.what: Administrative instruction assigning astronomical matters to Gauss and allowing a collection to be handed over to Prof. Harding (Göttingen observatory administration)

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries no mathematics, only an administrative note about the division of astronomical duties and collections between Gauss and Harding at Göttingen. It is of mild biographical interest only.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 should probably begin 'Alles, was in die Astronomie u. die verwandten' rather than 'Was[?] nur[?] in der Astronomie u. den verwandten'.
'zur Besorgung[?]': the image looks more like 'zur Besorgen' or 'zur Besorgung'; the meaning is the same.
'die Sammlung[?] aber[?]': 'Sammlung' is plausible; the next word may be 'auch' rather than 'aber'.
Line 5 opening 'auch[?]' may instead read 'nach'; the final word reads like 'stiftenden'.
The signature is a single flourished initial, likely 'H'. Attribution (e.g. to Heyne) is uncertain.
